hints: Focus on what happens to atomic size and number of electrons as you go down Group 17 from chlorine to iodine.
Remember that larger atoms form longer bonds, but also have more electrons to create stronger temporary dipoles between molecules.
Link stronger intermolecular forces to higher boiling points, and weaker, longer covalent bonds to lower bond energies, then check which graph matches.
walkthrough:
**Recall what changes down Group 17**

Think of going from $\text{Cl}_2$ to $\text{Br}_2$ to $\text{I}_2$. The atoms get bigger because extra shells are added. They also have many more electrons.

Trend down group: atomic radius increases, number of electrons increases.

**Predict the four properties**

Bigger atoms mean the covalent bond in $\text{X}_2$ gets longer and weaker. More electrons mean stronger London dispersion (van der Waals) forces between $\text{X}_2$ molecules.

So: bond length increases, van der Waals strength increases, boiling point of $\text{X}_2$ increases, bond energy of $\text{HX}$ decreases.

**Match to the graphs**

Only the graph showing an increase from $\text{Cl}_2$ to $\text{Br}_2$ to $\text{I}_2$ for strength of van der Waals forces fits the true trend. The other three graphs show the opposite direction to reality.

options.A: Incorrect. Bond length in $\text{X}_2$ increases down the group, not decreases. As atomic radius increases from Cl to I, the nuclei are further apart, so $\text{Cl}_2 < \text{Br}_2 < \text{I}_2$ for bond length. The graph shows a decrease.
options.B: Correct. Strength of van der Waals (London dispersion) forces increases from $\text{Cl}_2$ to $\text{Br}_2$ to $\text{I}_2$. More electrons and a larger, more polarisable electron cloud give stronger temporary dipoles, which is why boiling point also increases down the group.
options.C: Incorrect. Boiling point of $\text{X}_2$ increases down the group, not decreases. Stronger van der Waals forces need more energy to separate the molecules, so $\text{I}_2$ has the highest boiling point. The graph shows a decrease.
options.D: Incorrect. Bond energy of $\text{HX}$ decreases from $\text{HCl}$ to $\text{HBr}$ to $\text{HI}$, not increases. The H-X bond gets longer with poorer orbital overlap as X gets larger, so it gets weaker. The graph shows an increase.
